title: Contributing to birddog
text: Three public verbs : read_* (ingest), sniff_* (detect/measure), plot_* (visualize). Helpers: is_*, validate_*. detect_, filter_, get_ new exports. Two noun families: sniff_groups_* operates stock (groups point time); sniff_trajectory_* operates flow (temporal objects). word trajectory always singular function names. tr::/trN label grammar belongs exclusively flow partition. Stock plots always plot_groups_* (singular plot_group_* prefix retired). Pipeline-object contract: first argument every function object produced previous pipeline stage. Every sniff_trajectory_* analysis function takes flow object. Every plot_* takes output matching sniff_* recompute (one convenience exception, plot_trajectory_lines_* family, named rule 4). Flexible entry, strict core: two entry points trajectory layer, sniff_trajectory_dag() sniff_trajectory_braid(), accept lineage list (sniff_groups_lineage() output), docs_per_group, (flow) dag — resolved duck-typing one internal coercer as_trajectory_dag(). Downstream analysis functions demand exact flow class, two deliberate conveniences: sniff_trajectory_confluence() shares entry-point duck-typing (flow, dag, lineage, docs_per_group), plot_trajectory_lines_2d() / plot_trajectory_lines_3d() coerce loose input flow build confluence internally conf supplied. Algorithms detectors, arguments: future detection algorithm new sniff_trajectory_<algo>(dag, ...) consumes birddog_dag returns object passing validate_flow() (contract: trajectories, tree, graph, docs_per_group, last_year) inheriting contract class: class = c("birddog_<algo>", "birddog_flow", "list"). S3 dispatches every contract method (subset(), print(), future ones) new detectors free. method= dumping-ground argument. “Flow” names object kind, algorithm (stock vs flow: groups stock, trajectories flow): every detector returns flow — temporal decomposition DAG trajectories plus confluence tree. canonical detector sniff_trajectory_braid() carries object’s name; internal algorithm (mutual dominance today) may improved major version without renaming, named variants pin specific algorithms. validate_flow() contract’s authoritative checker. Stable label grammar public contract: cNgN (group), y<YYYY><cNgN> (group-year node), tr::<cNgN> (central), trN (absorbed). Documented ?birddog never changed within major version. Lifecycle discipline (2.0.0 onward): 2.0.0 one pre-launch hard break, justified absence users protect. 2.0.0 rule strict: new exports start experimental, promoted stable one CRAN cycle; anything removed goes deprecate_warn() -> deprecate_stop() -> deletion, never silently (lifecycle package added first needed). Breaking changes major versions. Number rules: noun verb’s direct object takes natural number (sniff_groups() finds many; sniff_network() builds one). Layer prefixes fixed number: groups_ (plural, stock-layer brand) trajectory_ (singular, attributive — trajectory flow like citation network). head noun takes natural number (_attributes, _hubs plural; _dag, _flow, _lineage singular; _dynamics plurale tantum). plural NEVER distinguishes scope: one-vs-argument (target =, n_routes =) map(), never trailing “s” — 1.x formation()/formations() trap banned permanently.

title: Introduction to birddog
text: birddog helps detect emergence trace trajectories scientific literature patents. reads datasets OpenAlex Web Science (WoS), builds citation-based networks, identifies groups, summarizes dynamics. stable release CRAN. development version available GitHub: https://github.com/roneyfraga/birddog.

title: Introduction to birddog
code: # stable version (CRAN) install.packages("birddog")  # development version (GitHub) # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("roneyfraga/birddog") library(birddog)

title: Introduction to birddog
text: birddog supports two main data sources: OpenAlex: browser search CSV export, API via openalexR. Web Science: multiple export formats (.bib, .ris, plain-text .txt, tab-delimited .txt).

title: Introduction to birddog
code: library(openalexR)  # Fetch works from OpenAlex API url_api <- "https://api.openalex.org/works?page=1&filter=primary_location.source.id:s121026525"  openalexR::oa_request(query_url = url_api) |>   openalexR::oa2df(entity = "works") |>   birddog::read_openalex(format = "api") ->   M  # Or from a CSV export M <- birddog::read_openalex("path/to/openalex-export.csv", format = "csv")

title: Introduction to birddog
code: # BibTeX M <- birddog::read_wos("path/to/savedrecs.bib", format = "bib")  # RIS M <- birddog::read_wos("path/to/savedrecs.ris", format = "ris")  # Plain text M <- birddog::read_wos("path/to/savedrecs.txt", format = "txt-plain-text")  # Tab-delimited M <- birddog::read_wos("path/to/savedrecs.txt", format = "txt-tab-delimited")

text: sniff_trajectory_dynamics() computes growth, novelty, recruitment destination indicators per trajectory, classifies one dynamic state. Emergence: central trajectory growing fast high share recent papers. Convergence: intermediate trajectory whose terminal cohort concentrates single central one. Divergence: intermediate trajectory whose cohort scatters across several. Dormancy: central trajectory stalled, intermediate one whose cohort mostly drops network. Central trajectories classified maturity.

"finals" draws central backbones (inflow spines, tributaries hidden); "intermediary" draws tributary streams (ribbons, central spines hidden). single central traj_id (e.g. "tr::c1g1") draws central's tributaries; vector central ids (e.g. c("tr::c1g1", "tr::c1g5")) draws selected centrals stacked. single central streams coloured per tributary; otherwise per destination central. single intermediate trajectory id (e.g. "tr3") switches focus view: feeders merge left (fed ) finals terminal cohort reached fan right (fed). depth many confluence levels upstream roots draw; NULL (default) means whole forest target = NULL, just direct feeders (1) one targets given. Set e.g. depth = 2 expand target view feeders--feeders. min_n Minimum papers tributary must transfer absorber counted; pruned drawing river width, together upstream subtree (default 5). min_prop Minimum share tributary's cohort must transfer (default 0.05); guards incidental trickles. min_total_size Minimum total size tributary (distinct paper count across years) drawn (default 0, filter); prunes small lineages upstream subtree, complementing min_n (gates transfer, trajectory's size). min_duration_years Minimum lifespan years tributary (last year minus first year, plus one) drawn (default 0, filter); use drop short-lived lineages. width_range Half-width range c(floor, max) y-data units (lanes spaced 1 apart, keep max ~0.5 avoid overlap). widest stream reaches max; every band least floor, thin streams stay visible. Default c(0, 0.42) strictly proportional (floor); positive floor (e.g. c(0.05, 0.45)) lifts small streams, raising max thickens everything. Note lane-fraction units, pixel sizes like marker_range. label_terminal Label content final (terminal) trajectories: "id_count" (default) tr::cNgN (size), "id" tr::cNgN, NULL hide . count central's final-year size (remains final community), matching plot_trajectory_lines_3d(), lifetime total. label_intermediary Label content intermediate (tributary) trajectories: "id_count" (default) trN (n), "id" trN, NULL hide . n tributary's documents end target final (destination count plot_trajectory_lines_3d()) – single target single-target view, else tributary's dominant central – trunk transfer. Objects without destination data fall back trN (n/cohort). label_terminal_size Text size final (terminal) labels (default 4.5). label_intermediary_size Text size intermediate (tributary) labels (default 4). labels_text Optional data.frame columns id text mapping central group ids (cNgN) descriptions; supplied bottom legend tr::cNgN: description added (plot_trajectory_dag()). NULL (default) adds legend. legend_ncol Number columns labels_text legend; NULL (default) lets ggplot choose. palette Optional named colour vector overriding default hues (keyed destination central /multi view, else tributary traj_id). axis_text_size Font size x-axis (year) tick labels; NULL (default) keeps theme default. year_range Optional c(, ) years fixing time axis (plot_trajectory_lines_2d()), short confluence can share window longer one. NULL (default) fits drawn rivers; wider range extends axis (never drops data). Ignored single-intermediate focus view. show_secondary Draw faint links tributary finals terminal cohort fed, beyond dominant one merges (default TRUE). tributary's papers can land several final groups; forest keeps dominant, links reveal rest. drawn spines ribbons shown destination central view (-view several selected centrals, single-central view). Needs destinations field sniff_trajectory_confluence(). secondary_min_prop Minimum share tributary's terminal cohort must reach secondary final link drawn (default 0.2); raise keep strongest secondary destinations. smooth Gaussian-smooth stream outlines (default TRUE): central spine's cumulative inflow tributary's width follow ~1-year low-pass edges flow brush strokes instead kinked polygons. FALSE keeps raw year--year steps. title Plot title; NULL (default) derives one target.

text: function calculates normalized Shannon entropy (Pielou's evenness index) based Shannon's information theory (Shannon, 1948). temporal scope keyword data depends mode parameter: annual: entropy keywords published specific year. Values tend high (near 1) since within-year distributions typically even. cumulative: entropy keywords published year. Shows long-term trends thematic concentration keyword pool grows. rolling: entropy sliding window recent years. Entropy values range 0 1, : 0 indicates minimal diversity (one dominant keyword) 1 indicates maximal diversity (keywords equally frequent) sudden increase entropy may signal emergence new research topics, decrease suggests thematic convergence.
